title: French Quarter bands Gabriel booked, Tony Pesina and the Johnsons
summary: He was the first Black band in the French Quarter, booked bands for clubs, and started Tucker Cole and Laverne Smith.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Some of them did it. When they come to Elmore, Elmore told them I'd be damned if I'm doing it. And she tried for her doing this to get it done. Uh-huh. But they wouldn't do it at our place. The doghouse had it for a while. And, uh, Puffy House and them had shoes there. They had a little place, Searrow. Searrow's in Fernhorn. Biamble between Bourbon and Royal, I think it was. I worked in there for him. And I also was booking bands in there for him. I supplied it one time, I was the only black band out in the French quarters. And, uh, Howard would play sometime, but regular bands, no.
Tiro Calico, was that the guy? I forgot. A little short guy.

Yeah, a little short Italian fella. Gray hair. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. And, uh, and everybody saw what a good band we had. And we was there on time every night. And they used to come around to me and ask, can they get a band, could I have a band like me. And I must have put about five or six different bands out there in the French quarters. Yeah. Well, Cole, Tucker Cole, he passed away in Chicago. Now he was stranded here in New Orleans some time ago. And I started him out in the French quarters. I started Laverne Smith out in the French quarters, at Tony Pesina's place. See, Tony Pesina, we come up in the same neighborhood. He was around, his dad had a grocery on Bianville and Miro, and I was at the next corner, the Cornine Miro.
You talking about which Tony Pesina's place?
He used to have a place on, uh, just off of, what did you call it? Just off of Bourbon Street, the gay place he had. Toulouse. Toulouse, yeah.
He used to have a couple places.
Yeah, and he went somewhere else. He had a woman, Johnson, this woman who played a kid. Gracie. Gracie, yeah. They all went, the whole family I think ended up out in California.
Plaz Johnson, one of our sons. They were doing good out in California the last I heard.
